answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consider a ocean as the anchor of the cost.
